snippets.text: Salvador Dalí House Museum was for decades the home of the Catalan artist, who bought up a string of fishing huts and joined them to form his eccentrically decorated seaside retreat.
The hiking trail Camí de Ronda traces the shoreline of the Costa Brava. The section that runs between Sa Riera and Sa Tuna is especially picturesque.
Jardins de Cap Roig, on an idyllic perch above El Golfet beach, features a sculpture garden and a medieval-style castle, and is home to more than 800 plant species.
The Bay of Roses, a vast stretch of white sand beach, is a popular spot for windsurfing.
Perched above the town of Begur, the stone ruins of the 11th-century Castell de Begur fortress offer sweeping views all the way to the Pyrenees.
Oli Bar is a new restaurant and wine bar with a cozy, candle-lit atmosphere, housed in a centuries-old olive oil mill.
In Begur’s old town, the specialty coffee shop Fitzroy Café doubles as a bar in the evenings, when it serves beer from local producers and natural wine.
Marítim Bar is a legendary beachfront institution in the town of Cadaqués dating back to 1935, counting Dalí and other art and literary figures among its visitors.
The day-to-night Bar Casino in Cadaqués is a popular spot for breakfast, with crusty bread rolls stuffed with Ibérico ham served on its beachfront terrace.
The late-night hotspot Cafe de la Habana is the go-to bar for live music in Cadaqués, with a long list of rums to keep the party going.
Ultramar is a waterfront restaurant in L’Escala with panoramic views along the coast and a wide variety of Catalan vermouths.
Patisseria Can Cabrisas is a century-old Cadaqués bakery renowned for its tap de Cadaqués, a cork-shaped sponge cake that’s been baked in the town since the 1700s.
Begur’s Casa Juanita is a cozy spot for authentic Catalan dishes, specializing in grilled fish and meat.

The seafront store Pepa has been a must-visit for fashionable travelers to Cadaqués since the 1970s, today stocking smaller Catalan brands alongside international designers like Jacquemus and Acne Studios.
The Cadaqués-founded swimwear brand Polonio has two stores in its hometown, where shoppers can find colorful trunks, bikinis and ready-to-wear pieces inspired by Mediterranean summer living.

Can Set is a pint-sized guesthouse in Cadaqués with six stylishly appointed rooms and its own cafe downstairs — a popular spot for long, lazy lunches by the sea. Rooms start at around 230 euros, or about $268.

Parador de Aiguablava was built in the 1960s on a pine-covered peninsula overlooking Aiguablava beach, about a 10-minute drive from Begur. Renovated in 2020, it is still a hub of mid-century chic and boasts a collection of more than 200 works by Catalan artists. Rooms start at ar

WeCamp has three sites along the Costa Brava — in Cadaqués, Santa Cristina and Cala Montgó — each with a range of glamping-style tents and wooden cabins available to rent. Bell tents from roughly €52 a night.

mentions.display: Making Feminist Art Before She Knew the Term

snippets.text: Making Feminist Art Before She Knew the Term: Wen Hui, the Chinese dancer, choreographer and filmmaker, “didn’t think in those terms” when she was young. Now, she said, “I’m more relaxed, more clear on what I want to do.”
America’s Birthday: Institutions around the country are preparing for the nation’s 250th anniversary, even in the face of political crosswinds.
Smelly Ants: A new exhibition at the Bruce Museum in Greenwich, Conn., gives visitors a whiff, from “chocolate-y” to stinky blue cheese.
